short: A restless, consolidating emperor who chose fixed frontiers over further conquest and toured the empire in person.
full:
Hadrian's succession on 11 August 117 CE was contested enough that four senior senators were executed soon after on suspicion of plotting against him, a stain he never fully lived down with the Senate. He reversed Trajan's eastern conquests as indefensible and spent much of his twenty-one-year reign travelling the provinces in person, an unusual practice for an emperor, overseeing construction and border works including the wall across northern Britain that bears his name.

Hadrian formalised the practice of adoptive succession, first naming Lucius Aelius and, after his death, adopting the senator Antoninus on condition that Antoninus in turn adopt both Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus — arranging two generations of succession in advance. He died on 10 July 138 CE after a long illness, having spent his final years increasingly unpopular at home despite the frontiers he had secured abroad.
